rules.statement: When the time for the performance of an obligation is fixed, the breach may well be considered as occurring when the performance does not take place within the time so fixed. However, if there is no fixed date but only an obligation to do any act within a reasonable interval after a given date, there cannot be said to be a breach unless there has been a refusal either on demand or otherwise to perform the obligation, or unless the person liable has in some way disabled himself from performing the contract.
rules.supporting_quote: When the time for the performance of an obligation is fixed so that there can be a definite starting point for the running of the period of prescription, the breach may well, in ordinary circumstances, be considered as occurring when the performance does not take place within the time so fixed. But when there is no fixed date for the performance, but there is only an obligation to do any act within a reasonable interval after a given date, there cannot be said to be a breach, unless there has been a refusal either on demand or otherwise to perform the obligation, or unless the person liable has in some way disabled himself from performing the contract.
